title: Incident First Responder Checklist and Training Syllabus
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This document combines a concise "first responder" checklist (for use when a page is triggered or a pager alerts) with a structured on-call training syllabus and simulation plan. It is intended for new on-call engineers, incident commanders, and SRE mentors. The goal is to reduce time-to-containment, standardize communications, and build muscle memory through regular game days.

Scope and audience
-------------------
- Scope: services hosted in Redwood’s public regions and Dedicated fleets. Private deployments should follow the same play model but reference customer-specific runbooks.
- Audience: on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), on-call mentors, and engineering managers.

Objectives
----------
1. Provide an immediately actionable checklist for the first 15 minutes of any page.
2. Define a repeatable training syllabus for ramping new responders to independent on-call status.
3. Provide templates for internal and customer communications.
4. Define a quarterly simulation (game day) plan to validate skills and runbooks.

Roles and ownership
-------------------
- First responder: acknowledges the page and begins triage (usually on-call engineer).
- Incident commander (IC): coordinates cross-team activity when an incident is declared (rotating responsibility per escalation matrix).
- SRE mentor: shadow for junior responders; runs post-game-day retrospective.
- Communications lead: drafts customer and internal updates during major incidents.

First 15-minute first-responder checklist (use immediately)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge and gather context (0-1 min)
   - Acknowledge the pager in PagerDuty and Slack (#sre-pager).
   - Open the incident signal in the status dashboard (/status) and check active alerts.
   - Capture high-level impact: number of customers affected, traffic region, services impacted.
2) Quick blast radius and safety (1-4 min)
   - Check service health dashboards (Prometheus / Grafana links in runbook header).
   - If traffic spike or job backlog, set temporary throttles/redirects if documented in runbook.
   - If suspecting job queue or database saturation, pause background jobs where safe.
3) Gather immediate evidence (4-8 min)
   - Collect the last 3 minutes of logs from the primary service and gateway (use the /runbook/collect-logs script).
   - Check error budget burn rate and SLO dashboard (SLO: 99.9% p99 latency per-route; error budget threshold 2% per week).
4) Rapid mitigation (8-12 min)
   - If a single recent deploy is implicated, rollback to the previous tagged release per Deploy rollback SOP (see section 'Rollback steps').
   - If an upstream dependency is failing, switch to fallback model or cached response (see Smart routing policy runbook).
5) Declare and escalate if needed (12-15 min)
   - If impact is customer-visible and expanding, declare an incident and notify IC.
   - Use the escalation matrix below to notify on-call managers and product owner.

Triage flow (decision ladder)
-----------------------------
1) Is traffic or latency outside SLAs? Yes -> identify impacted route and scope. No -> monitor and re-evaluate in 15 minutes.
2) Is error rate increasing? Yes -> fetch recent deploys and lead engineers.
3) Is there a clear mitigation documented? Yes -> apply mitigation and validate. No -> escalate to IC.

Escalation matrix (abbreviated)
-------------------------------
| Severity | Who to page first | After 10 minutes | After 30 minutes |
|----------|-------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Sev-1 (complete outage) | Service on-call + IC | SRE manager | CTO + CS Director |
| Sev-2 (partial outage / degraded latency) | Service on-call | Service lead | SRE manager |
| Sev-3 (localized error) | Service on-call | On-call mentor | - |

Communication templates
-----------------------
Internal incident status (Slack pinned update)
1) Title: [INC][Sev-1] API region us-east: Elevated 500s
2) Current impact: ~40% of requests in us-east returning 500; pages from gateway.
3) Actions taken: Rolled back api-service v2.4.1 -> v2.4.0; rate-limited batch ingestion; investigating DB proxy.
4) Next update: 15:20 UTC or on status change.

Customer status page template (short):
- Headline: Degraded API responses in us-east (partial outage)
- Impact: Some API requests returning errors for customers in US-East.
- What we are doing: Rolling back a recent release and diverting traffic to fallback model.
- ETA: We expect substantive recovery within 45 minutes; updates every 30 minutes.

Postmortem and evidence checklist (minimum required fields)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Incident summary (one-line)
- Timeline (UTC timestamps)
- Root cause hypothesis and confirmed root cause
- Contributing factors (human, tooling, process)
- What we did to mitigate and why
- Corrective actions and owners (with target dates)
- Customer impact and communications record (links to status page updates)
- Metrics appendices: SLO burn, error rates, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99)

On-call training syllabus (4-week onboarding plan)
------------------------------------------------
Week 0 (preflight)
- Read: This doc, service runbooks, incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026.
- Access: Ensure PagerDuty, Slack, Grafana, and runbook editor access.
Week 1 (observation & shadow)
- Shadow three on-call shifts with a mentor.
- Complete a checklist of 10 common alerts and their mitigations in the sandbox environment.
Week 2 (guided response)
- Respond to low-severity pages with mentor oversight.
- Run the runbook play: simulate a dependent-service failure.
Week 3 (independent response + review)
- Handle shifts independently for at least 3 rotations.
- Draft a post-incident summary for a simulated incident and present to SRE mentor.

Hands-on labs and scripts
------------------------
- collect-logs.sh: gathers last 10 minutes of logs from service and gateway (examples in runbook header).
- simulate-latency.py: local tooling to reproduce slow downstream responses in test environment.
- rollback.sh <service> <tag>: automated rollback helper with health checks.

Quarterly game-day plan (90–120 minutes)
----------------------------------------
- Frequency: quarterly per platform team; cross-team exercise annually.
- Structure: 15-min setup, 45-min injected incident (several correlated failures), 30-min mitigation period, 30-min retrospective.
- Success criteria: containment within 60 minutes for Sev-2 scenarios; validated communication cadence and status page updates.

SLO and metrics to monitor during training and real incidents
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Availability SLO: 99.9% regional availability (rolling 7-day).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for read routes; p99 < 800ms.
- Alerting thresholds: p95 latency > 350ms for 5m -> Pager duty; error rate > 0.5% -> page.

Runbook governance and cadence
-----------------------------
- Every runbook has an owner listed in the header and a review_date field.
- Owners must triage reviewer comments within 7 business days.
- Annual runbook drill: owners run a 20-minute walkthrough in the team retro.

Templates and artifacts directory
-------------------------------
- Slack templates: /confluence/templates/incident-slack-updates
- Status page updates: /confluence/templates/status-pages
- Postmortem template: /confluence/templates/postmortem-standard

Appendices
----------
A. Quick CLI snippets
- Collect logs: ./collect-logs.sh --service api-service --minutes 10 --out /tmp/incident-logs.tar.gz
- Trigger rollback: ./rollback.sh api-service v2.4.0

B. Escalation contact matrix (internal)
- SRE manager: sre-manager@redwood.ai
- CS Director: cs-director@redwood.ai
- On-call schedule: https://pagerduty.com/schedules/redwood-inference/oncall

C. Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
Q: When should I declare an incident?
A: Declare if the issue is customer facing (errors or latency above SLOs) or when mitigation requires cross-team coordination.

D. How to use this document in practice
- Keep this doc as a lightweight checklist; meatier, service-specific steps belong in each service runbook.
- During a real incident, paste the slack template into #incident-ops and pin it for visibility.
